STEP 1 - Scene: A single whole red-and-yellow apple sitting on a white square plate, photographed from above (near top-down, slight angle). It is a fruit snack, not a full meal.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate's longest undistorted width is roughly 24 cm across the diagonal-free sides; I'll treat it as a ~24 cm square-ish plate. Area of a 24 cm plate ≈ 3.14 x (12)^2 ≈ 452 cm^2 (equivalent circle). The apple is about 8 cm in diameter by comparison with the plate (roughly one third of the plate width).

STEP 3 - Items: One whole apple (red/yellow skin, stem cavity visible). No sauce or oil.

STEP 4 - Area: Apple covers its circular footprint, about 50 cm^2 (8 cm diameter), which is roughly 11% of the plate area.

STEP 5 - Volume: An apple is roughly spherical; height ≈ 7.5 cm, so volume ≈ (4/3)π(4)^3 ≈ 268 ml. Using the footprint envelope, 50 cm^2 x 7 cm ≈ 350 ml, but a sphere is closer, so I use about 270 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Apple is a fruit with density close to 0.85 g/ml as a whole fruit (it is mostly water with air pockets in the core), giving about 230 g. Typical medium apple weighs 150–200 g, and this one looks medium-to-large, so I settle on about 180 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Apple, raw, ~52 kcal/100 g. 180 g x 0.52 ≈ 94 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A single medium apple at roughly 180 g and ~95 kcal is plausible for what is visible and matches typical nutrition data.
